mistakes.name: Leaning back at contact
mistakes.plain_english: Your upper body is leaning behind your hips when you strike the ball. This sends passes upward and reduces accuracy.
mistakes.root_cause: Plant foot is behind the ball instead of beside it.
mistakes.correction: Move your plant foot so it lands beside the ball, not behind it. Drive your chest forward at contact.

mistakes.name: Avoiding the weaker foot
mistakes.plain_english: You are always using your stronger foot even when your weaker foot would be easier. This makes your play predictable.
mistakes.root_cause: Insufficient weak-foot practice creates a confidence gap.
mistakes.correction: Dedicate 30% of all passing practice to your weaker foot.

mistakes.name: Stopping the kicking motion at contact
mistakes.plain_english: Your leg stops moving after it hits the ball. This causes the ball to deviate from your intended target.
mistakes.root_cause: Tension in the kicking leg reduces follow-through.
mistakes.correction: Mentally commit to kicking through the ball. Finish with your kicking foot pointing at the target.

mistakes.name: Not scanning before receiving
mistakes.plain_english: You receive the ball without looking up first, so you have no information about where to pass. You slow the game down.
mistakes.root_cause: Ball-watching habit — head follows the ball instead of scanning the pitch.
mistakes.correction: Look up at least twice before the ball reaches you. Decide your pass before it arrives.

mistakes.name: First touch too heavy
mistakes.plain_english: The ball bounces too far away when you receive it. You lose time and position recovering it.
mistakes.root_cause: Foot or body is too rigid at contact — not cushioning the ball.
mistakes.correction: Relax your receiving foot. Let the ball come to you — cushion it rather than stopping it dead.
